search_keyword: RSI(2) mean reversion trading strategy Larry Connors rules
page_summary: StockCharts ChartSchool article on Larry Connors RSI(2) mean-reversion strategy: (1) trend filter = 200-day SMA (long only above, short only below); (2) entry trigger = RSI(2) closing below 5 for longs (below 10 tested, 5 found stronger) / above 95 for shorts; (3) enter next open or before close; (4) exit long on close above 5-day SMA (exit short on close below 5-day SMA); Connors found stops hurt backtested performance but flags this raises drawdown risk.
notes: Long-only variant (no shorting, per SAFETY.md/loop convention -- prior strategies here are also long-only) tested this iteration: 200d SMA trend gate + RSI(2) dip-buy entry + 5d SMA cross exit.

search_keyword: turn of month effect stock returns strategy rules first last trading days
page_summary: TapeScript blog on the turn-of-the-month (Ultimo) effect, citing Ariel (1987) and McConnell & Xu (2008, Financial Analysts Journal): from 1926-2005 essentially all of the US stock markets average positive return occurred in a 4-trading-day window per month -- the last trading day of the month plus the first three trading days of the next month. Rest of month averaged near zero. Confirmed across 34 other countries. Driven by predictable month-end cash flows (paychecks, 401k contributions, fund rebalancing).
notes: Concrete, parameter-light calendar-anomaly hypothesis: long only during last trading day of month + first N trading days of next month, flat otherwise. Testable directly on SPY/QQQ (equity) and BTC/USDT/ETH/USDT (crypto, to see if a cash-flow-driven equity effect transfers to a market without payroll/401k cycles).

search_keyword: overnight effect stock returns close to open outperform intraday anomaly strategy
page_summary: STOXX blog (Hamish Seegopaul) analyzing the overnight return anomaly in EURO STOXX 50 / iShares EUE ETF, Jan 2016-Oct 2025: overnight (prev close-to-open) return 12.9% p.a. vs total ETF return ~8% p.a., with intraday (open-to-close) actually NEGATIVE at -4.3% p.a. After 2bp/day round-trip trading costs, net overnight return falls to 7.3% p.a. (still below buy-and-hold). Cites Boyarchenko/Larsen/Whelan 2023 The Overnight Drift (Review of Financial Studies) and Haghani/Ragulin/Dewey 2024 Night Moves as academic sources. Concrete testable strategy: hold only overnight (close-to-open), flat during the trading session.
notes: Directly testable with daily OHLCV (has open+close columns) via data/loaders.py: position = long only from prior close to today open (approximated as holding overnight-return-only exposure), flat during the day session. Also testing crypto as a falsification check since crypto trades 24/7 with no discrete close/open session boundary equivalent to equities.

search_keyword: Donchian channel breakout trend following strategy rules backtest crypto
page_summary: Secuora original-research backtest of classic Turtle-style 20-bar Donchian channel breakout (bidirectional long+short, no trend filter, 1.5xATR(14) stop, 2R target) on BTC/ETH 1h candles, Jun 2025-Jun 2026, Binance data. Net-losing on both symbols: BTC profit factor 0.76, MDD 52.2%, net -51.1%; ETH profit factor 0.97 (near breakeven), MDD 27.3%, net -9.7%. Overall win rate 33.9%, 803 trades. Exact rules given: entry = close beyond 20-bar high/low channel (cross semantics, fires once on breakout not every bar beyond); explicitly attributes poor performance to breakout systems only working when the instrument actually trends (no filter to skip choppy/ranging periods).
notes: Concrete, parameter-specified breakout rule (N-bar Donchian channel entry/exit) with an honest documented failure mode (bidirectional + no trend filter = whipsaw losses in chop). Testable hypothesis: restricting to long-only breakouts above a 200d SMA trend filter (daily bars, not hourly) should remove most of the counter-trend whipsaw that hurt the raw bidirectional version.

search_keyword: short term reversal 5 day return equity anomaly strategy rules quantifiedstrategies
page_summary: Quantpedia summary of the short-term reversal anomaly (Jegadeesh 1990 lineage): stocks with low returns over the past week/month earn positive abnormal returns the following week/month, and vice versa (overreaction + liquidity-provision explanation, Nagel Evaporating Liquidity). Cross-sectional long-short across a stock universe (buy losers, sell winners), profitable net of costs only when restricted to larger-cap names due to high turnover. search_keyword: gap fade opening gap reversal strategy rules stocks backtest
page_summary: DayTradingToolkit guide on the gap fade strategy: overnight gaps driven by retail attention/sentiment tend to reverse (fade) intraday once daytime arbitrageurs trade against the overnight order-flow imbalance, per academic research cited: Berkman/Koch/Tuttle/Zhang (2012, original finding: positive overnight returns followed by intraday reversals), Aboody/Even-Tov/Lehavy/Trueman (2018, confirmed with expanded methodology), Akbas/Boehmer/Jiang/Koch (2022, tug-of-war framing between overnight noise traders and daytime arbitrageurs). The articles specific setup (minute-level pre-market volume screening, opening-range entry triggers, intraday stop/target scaling) requires intraday/tick data this repos loaders (daily OHLCV via yfinance/ccxt) cannot provide, but the core academic finding -- overnight gap direction predicts an OPPOSITE intraday (open-to-close) return -- is directly testable at daily granularity using existing open/close columns.
notes: Adapted the daily-granularity-testable core of the academic finding: after a gap DOWN (open meaningfully below prior close), go long from open to close (intraday only), betting on a fade/reversal back up -- long-only per SAFETY.md, so only testing the gap-down-fade side (would require shorting to fade gap-ups). Distinct from 2026-09-03-007 (overnight_drift, which holds close-to-open) -- this holds open-to-close (the opposite sub-daily window) and is conditioned on a gap-down trigger rather than unconditional participation.

search_keyword: Bollinger Band squeeze breakout volatility contraction strategy rules backtest
page_summary: QuantifiedStrategies.com Bollinger Band squeeze strategy article: identifies squeeze via a bandwidth indicator (upper-band minus lower-band, e.g. 25-day lookback, 2 std) hitting unusually low values (volatility contraction/consolidation), then trades a breakout beyond the bands in the breakout direction, expecting trend continuation. search_keyword: SuperTrend indicator strategy rules ATR multiplier backtest crypto stocks
page_summary: Google AI-overview summary (web_search returned no results for this keyword, fell back to browser_exec Google search) of SuperTrend indicator core strategy rules: ATR period 10-14, multiplier 3 (default); SuperTrend line = ATR-based dynamic support/resistance band that flips direction; buy/long when price closes above the SuperTrend line and it flips from red(down) to green(up); exit/short when price closes below the line and it flips green to red; the line itself doubles as a trailing stop. Lower multiplier (2.0-2.5) = tighter stop/more signals/more whipsaw; higher multiplier (3.0-5.0) = wider stop, filters noise, better for volatile assets.
notes: Concrete parameterized rule (ATR(10 or 14) x multiplier 3, flip-based long/flat, line-as-trailing-stop) -- first ATR-volatility-band trend indicator tested in this repo, distinct from Donchian channel breakout (-008, pure price-level channel, no ATR) and from prior SMA/momentum trend filters (fixed lookback return/MA, not a volatility-adaptive band).

search_keyword: ADX trend strength filter strategy rules threshold backtest
page_summary: Google search snippets (web_search backend has been intermittently failing this trigger, used browser_exec Google search directly this time to save a retry) on ADX/DMI trend-strength filtering. Reddit r/algotrading and multiple sources converge on the same concrete rule: ADX must be above 25 AND +DI crosses above -DI for a long entry (classic Wilder DMI/ADX system); ADX below 20-25 signals range-bound/choppy conditions to sit out. TradingView snippet: a trade can qualify only when ADX is above the selected threshold (used as a trend-strength gate on top of another entry signal).
notes: Concrete, well-sourced, converging-across-multiple-sites rule: ADX(14)>25 AND +DI crosses above -DI for long entry, exit on -DI crossing above +DI (or ADX falling back below threshold). First DMI/ADX-directional-index strategy tested in this repo -- distinct from every prior trend/momentum construction (SMA, Bollinger, trailing-return momentum, RSI2, Donchian, MACD, SuperTrend, Keltner, 52wk-high) since ADX/DMI decomposes trend STRENGTH separately from trend DIRECTION.
